title: sre-weekly-ops-sync-notes-2026-03-19-draft
content:
SRE Weekly Ops Sync + Reliability Review (prep notes) - 2026-03-19

Attendees (planned): Jordan, Samira, Aisha, Miguel (optional), on-call rotation rep (TBD)
Time: 9:30am PT
Duration: 45min
Objective: quick status on SLOs/paging trends, review top incidents, align on short-term mitigation + owners for follow-ups

Agenda draft:
- 5m: Quick wins / shoutouts
- 10m: SLO health summary / alerts trend (past 7d vs 30d)
- 10m: Paging trends review + possible config changes to reduce noise
- 15m: Top incidents deep-dive (INC-2026-03-17 + ongoing thrashing on ded clusters)
- 5m: Action items + owners

Prep metrics to surface (I'll pull these before the sync):
- Error budget burn: hosting-api request success SLO (p99 latency, p95 latency), token-generation success rate SLO (serving-runtime)
- Pager counts by channel (pagerduty email vs mobile) last 7 days and last 30 days
- Number of SEV2/SEV3s this sprint and mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to resolve (MTTR)
- Top error types last 7 days (OOM, model load failures, 503s from autoscaler, networking transient errors)

Current quick summary (raw notes):
- Error budget: hosting-api p99 latency used ~ 11% this week (good). Token-generation success rate dipping to 97.3% on 2026-03-17 during incident (target 99.5%). Need to show spline chart for last 14d.
- Paging: 22 pages last 7 days (baseline 9). Spike concentrated on 2026-03-17 (15 pages). Nighttime noise increased due to retried autoscaler errors (see incidents).
- MTTA: median 3m (still OK), MTTR: median 28m (inflated by the model-serving OOM incident where we did a staged restart and rollback).

Top incidents to review:
1) INC-2026-03-17: model-serving OOM -> degraded token-generation on Hosted pool \n   - Timeline (brief): 02:11 UTC sudden surge of OOMs on dedicated worker pool for model-v2-compatible variants, 02:13 first pager, by 02:18 we throttled traffic and rolled back to model-v1-compatible variant, 02:27 full recovery after rolling restart of 6 nodes. Total impact ~16m with error budget hit for token-generation SLO.
   - Root cause (working hypothesis): memory leak in KV cache eviction path exposed by a small regression in runtime kernel selection (recent change rolled last week). Under head-of-line batching + long context sessions, cache growth not bounded properly.
   - Immediate mitigations applied: limited batch size to 4 for impacted pool, force eviction interval shortened, rollback of runtime change to previous kernel selection policy.
   - Follow-ups / owners:
     * Jordan: write short postmortem draft + timeline (due EOD Fri) - JIRA SRE-412
     * Eng/Serving Runtime: reproduce locally with stress harness; validate cache metrics and GC paths - owner: Miguel - target: 2026-03-23
     * Infra: add a safety OOM kill metric to combined alerting rule to auto-scale or pause new sessions - owner: Samira - target: 2026-03-26
     * Product/Console: flag affected customers and provide RC info for any SLA credits (CS coordination) - owner: Aisha/CS - target: 2026-03-20

2) Ongoing: autoscaler retry storms causing transient 503s during cold-start windows (reduced but persistent)
   - Notes: several small infra changes last month (kube autoscaler tuning) reduced freq by ~40% but still see bursts when traffic pattern has many small concurrent deploys or many low-qps clients returning simultaneously.
   - Possible mitigations to discuss: smoothing policy for burst detection, increase min pool for dedicated workloads during release windows, heuristics to defer non-critical background work during cold-start spikes.
   - Owner candidates: infra/platform-engineering (we should loop in Rafael and infra-oncall)

Paging trend analysis (thoughts):
- Noise sources to consider for reduction:
  * flaky external auth errors -> already filtered for noisy bots; need second pass on bot-exclusion rules (Samira?)
  * transient 503s due to autoscaler -> tune backoff + reduce pager severity for short-lived 503 bursts < 2min if self-healing
  * repeated application-level retries causing duplicate pages -> check client retry configs in SDK + recommend client-side linear backoff docs update

Proposed alert config changes (quick prototypes):
- Change severity mapping: short transient 5xx spikes < 2m and < X per minute -> alert as SEV3 (ticket), not immediate page. Need to be careful with true outages.
- Introduce composite alert: "OOM rate + cache mem growth" -> page only when both triggered to reduce noisy OOM symptom pages when not service-impacting.
- Add presentation to console: per-route recent OOMs and cache growth metric for operators to triage quickly.

Action items (to confirm in meeting):
- Aisha: notify CS & create customer impact summary (by 2026-03-20) - assign via shared incident doc link
- Jordan: postmortem draft + initial timeline (by EOD 2026-03-19)
- Miguel: reproduce and propose code fix for cache eviction (P0/P1 decision) (by 2026-03-23)
- Samira: propose alert tuning PR and bot-exclusion review (by 2026-03-26)
- Rafael/Infra: review autoscaler smoothing policy and min-pool suggestions (meeting invite)

Open questions for the sync:
- Do we have consensus on severity remapping for short transient 5xxs? Danger: could hide real intermittent failures.
- Should we temporarily increase min-pool for dedicated-hosted staging clusters during the next 2 weeks while we roll kernel-fix? Cost tradeoff vs risk?
- Any customers flagged by CS that need immediate escalation to Eng leadership? (I will surface if yes)

Notes / things to capture in postmortem template:
- Timeline with exact timestamps and commands issued (who executed rollback/restart)
- Root cause analysis (what changed in runtime/kernel selection and why it exposed leak)
- Why did autoscaler/monitoring not prevent escalation? (gaps in alerting thresholds or missing composite alerts)
- Corrective actions (code fix, monitoring/alerting changes, runbook updates)
- Preventive actions (load tests, stress harness, create regression test for KV cache growth)

Meeting output expectations:
- End of meeting: owners assigned for each follow-up with concrete due dates and JIRA links
- If consensus on alert tuning -> open PR with proposed threshold changes and add a canary in staging for 72h

Misc notes / scratch (to tidy before finalizing):
- Pull logs for 02:05-02:35 UTC across serving-runtime and infra-autoscaler (done? need to request from logging team if >30d retention)
- Validate that rollback was actually applied to all affected nodes (one node reported still on new kernel at 02:40 -> check)
- Add a small CSV of pager counts by hour to share with execs (if requested)

Draft email to CS (short):
- subject: "Incident update: token-generation degradation on 2026-03-17 (INC-2026-03-17)"
- body: high-level impact, mitigation steps, ETA for postmortem + how customers are being contacted. I'll draft and share for review.

End notes: this is a working draft — will tidy after Jordan adds timeline. Bring any logs you've pulled to the meeting.

-- Aisha
